programmes.show_description: In Sussex, Henry Cole and Simon O'Brien meet Bill and Annie, who have a penchant for Star Wars collectables and, most importantly - as far as Henry is concerned - motorbikes!
Jon and Julia Shorrock host at the four-star Derwent House B&B in West Sussex. Andy and Julian have concerns over their carpeted bathroom, and Peter can't get any hot water.
Peter and Sharron Sorsky welcome their rivals to their Liverpool home, Kirkby Park B&B. But the guests discover dust, hairs, stains and even a hole in the wall!
Andy and Julian Banner-Price host at the swanky Plas Dinas Country House in Eryri (Snowdonia), where they've allocated their guests the priciest rooms.
The final visit is to Annette McAnespie's Hazelwood Farm in Crake, Yorkshire, where she's lined up her idea of fun for her guests: a cycling tour. But not everyone is up for it...
It's been a week of waterworks, tall tales and breakfast scrambles, but who will end up with the prize? And will any of the B&Bers want to see each other again?
Brighton. Will medical editor and rapper Adam's abundant vegetables impress his guests as he serves a simple yet wholesome vegetarian menu? (Ep1/5)
Brighton. Copywriter Will is confident that his veggie menu will trump Adam's from the night before. But there are some fishy goings-on and Will's risotto is upstaged... (Ep2/5)
Brighton. Retired advertising sales director Gill hosts with a Middle Eastern menu and a fun dress code, on a night featuring unexpected revelations and some very honest feedback. (Ep3/5)
Brighton. Teacher and surfer Jo treats her guests to a tropical-themed evening featuring some hit-and-miss food, a dessert drama and a cheeky massage thrown in for good measure. (Ep4/5)
Brighton. Social worker Ruth serves up a Jewish-Irish fusion menu on a night featuring kitchen chaos, some unexpected veggies and a knicker-nicking, limelight-stealing cat. (Ep5/5)
The competition moves to France, where four sets of Brits compete to be crowned best value B&B. First host Lisanne Ashton hopes to impress with her rustic rural guest house, Les Chimeres.
In France, eccentric royalist Tony Horton and his Armenian wife Shou Shou provide an unusual mix of vinegar tasting and royal regalia at Le Manoir in the Dordogne.
In France, Shaun Baggs and his partner Patrick Weaver host at Le Clos Rabelais. There are high kicks, low blows and some unfavourable feedback.
George and Linda offer their guests 'a little slice of England' at the Moulin de la Civiere in Brittany, where one guest goes potty for the Victorian loos.
It's the final day in France. Tensions run high as the B&Bers discover how much they've been paid and settle some scores, before the winner is revealed.

programmes.show_description: In Windsor, Henry Cole finds an Austrian moped that's missing just one key item: an engine. And Simon O'Brien's taken with a fibreglass suit of armour called Ralph.
Melvyn and Sindy host at their sports car-themed B&B, The Pitstop, in Hertfordshire. But their guests are dubious about the satin sheets and the DIY breakfast.
Corporate couple Gill and Peter host at the four-star Victory at Mersea B&B in Essex, which has 26 staff. Melvyn finds a hole in the bed sheet and there's spilt coffee at breakfast.
It's Dave 'Butterfly' Botha's turn to host at his two-star establishment, Butterfly Paragliding B&B on the Isle of Wight, where he opts for a barbecue dinner despite the freezing weather.
Deborah and Wayne host at their B&B, Braddon Hall, in Torquay. But there are concerns over squeaky beds and mismatched typefaces, and allegations fly during an archery competition.
It's the final day and the B&Bers meet one last time to find out how much they've been paid. Gill and Peter bristle at their feedback and two underpayments, before the winner is announced.
Edinburgh. The first host, Christian radio DJ and gospel singer Eloho, hopes that her guests will sing her praises after her music-filled evening and traditional Nigerian fare. (Ep1/5)
Edinburgh. Cabin crew trainer Julie plans an evening of Scottish fine dining, including a hearty winter warmer, her grandmother's Cullen skink and a full Scottish pipe band. (Ep2/5)
Edinburgh. IT manager and occasional stand-up comic Ryan hosts with a menu designed by his friend who's a Michelin-starred chef. But Ryan has no idea how to cook any of it! (Ep3/5)
Edinburgh. Cabbie Jamie pulls out all the stops with a fine dining menu. But will he impress his guests with his choice of chat and a striptease during a silent disco? (Ep4/5)
Edinburgh. Business owner and socialite Maz hopes that her top-notch hosting skills, charm offensive and some fantastic fondue will win her the grand on the final night. (Ep5/5)
At Fountains Court Holistic Health Hotel in Scarborough, Helen Marriott offers her guests a chance to 'step off the planet' through essential breathing lessons and a soulful foot massage.
Sue Perkins welcomes her rivals to her Hull pub and B&B, The Whittington & Cat. The guests enjoy an afternoon of ice hockey but are puzzled by Sue's breakfast.
Khurram Saba hosts the third visit, at the Saba Hotel in London, where his guests are expecting big city chic, fancy food - and definitely not fish and chips for dinner...
Candida Leaver and Peter Starling host the final visit, at The Bower Inn in Bridgwater, where the group activity is willow-weaving and there are spooky tales at breakfast.
It's the final day of the competition and the B&Bers meet for the last time to air their grievances and discover how much they've been paid, before the winner is announced.
